# MM-P3-L3-SB01 Maintenance manual - Machining shot blast cabinet #1

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01

Scope
This manual defines the preventive maintenance tasks, methods, and acceptance criteria for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01). It applies to maintenance technicians and process engineers responsible for preserving part quality, safety, and equipment availability on line P3-L3. This document references related procedures and records as listed in the related documents section and supplements the operational controls in SOP-P3-L3-03.

Background and rationale
The cabinet provides controlled abrasive cleaning of machined castings prior to downstream handling. Key failure modes affecting part finish and cycle reliability include wear of the blast wheel components, loss of media volume, and contamination of recycled media. Regular inspection and adjustment reduce scrap and unplanned downtime, and preserve blast pattern consistency. The tasks below prioritize fast inspection of critical items and corrective actions that restore the system to known condition.

Related documents
- MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2
- SB-1022
- SOP-P3-L3-03

Tools and materials
- Hand tools as specified by the manufacturer and maintenance group; use only tools that match fastener head geometry and access profile.
- Torque wrench capable of achieving the required torque range for the blast wheel liner bolts.
- Media handling container and scale for inventory record entries.
- Replacement liner segments and gasket materials as listed in SB-1022.
- Personal protective equipment consistent with SOP-P3-L3-03.

Safety notes and controls
Follow lockout-tagout and isolation procedures defined in SOP-P3-L3-03 before entering the cabinet or exposing rotating assemblies. Verify energy isolation and test for stored energy. Use hearing protection and impact-rated eye protection while performing any test run or inspection with the cabinet energized. Ensure the cabinet door interlocks are validated during reassembly.

Procedure
The procedure is organized into inspection, service, and functional verification stages. Use the steady-state routines described here for scheduled preventive maintenance and after any corrective replacement of blast wheel or cabinet internals.

- Preparation
  - Secure isolation in accordance with SOP-P3-L3-03. Record the isolation action in the work order and maintenance log.
  - Confirm required replacement parts are staged per SB-1022 and review any previous findings in MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2.

- Inspection and cleaning
  - Open the cabinet access panel and visually inspect the blast wheel housing and liner surfaces for signs of uneven wear, cracking, or missing segments. Pay attention to the mating faces and seam locations.
  - Remove accumulated fines and dust from the media hopper and return lines. Capture and contain the fines for disposal per local waste procedure.
  - Inspect media quality in the hopper for contamination with tramp material or excessive fines. Segregate questionable media for analysis and possible replacement.

- Liner and wheel maintenance
  - Remove liner segments as needed to access the blast wheel assembly. Clean mating surfaces and prepare for reassembly.
  - When reinstalling liner segments, ensure all liner bolt threads are clean and free of media debris. Apply the required bolt clamp using the torque wrench set to the specified torque.
  - The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is 105 N·m.
  - Reinstall wheel housing covers and fasteners to restore the cabinet envelope.

- Media top-up and inventory
  - Verify media level in the hopper and compare to the media inventory record. Top up media as required to maintain consistent feed to the wheel.
  - The shot media top-up interval for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is 22 hours. Use this interval as the planning cadence for media checks and top-up activities in the CMMS.
  - Record media addition volumes and source lot identifiers in the maintenance log and link to production batches as required for traceability.

- Functional verification
  - Re-establish isolation controls and remove tagouts only when instructed by a qualified supervisor. Perform a guarded test run per SOP-P3-L3-03 and verify blast pattern uniformity on a verification panel or sacrificial coupon.
  - Inspect for abnormal vibration, unusual noise, or loose fasteners after the initial run. If any anomaly is detected, stop the machine and re-check mounting and liner fasteners.

Examples and troubleshooting guidance
- Example: If edge wear is concentrated on a single liner segment, inspect the wheel balance and orientation. Corrective action may include repositioning the wheel or replacing the affected liner segment per SB-1022.
- Example: If media consumption is excessive without corresponding process load increase, sample the media for fines and contamination. Replace contaminated media and document the findings in MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2.
- If a fastener is found loose during inspection, re-torque to the specified value and note the discrepancy in the work order. If repeat loosening occurs, escalate to engineering for a root cause analysis.

Records to keep
- Maintenance work order documenting tasks performed, parts replaced, and observations. Reference MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2 for historic trend data.
- Media inventory and top-up log with lot identifiers and date/time stamps consistent with CMMS entries. Link records to production batch numbers where required by SOP-P3-L3-03.
- Torque verification sheet showing the blast wheel liner bolt torque values recorded after reassembly.
- Inspection checklists and functional verification coupons stored per site record retention policy. Include any nonconformances raised and corrective actions taken.

Acceptance criteria
The cabinet is acceptable for return to service when all of the following conditions are met:
- Visual inspection shows liner segments properly seated and free of visible cracks or missing pieces.
- All blast wheel liner bolts hold the specified clamp and are recorded at the specified torque value.
- Media level and quality meet production specifications and the media top-up cadence is documented in the media log.
- Functional verification demonstrates uniform blast pattern, acceptable vibration, and no abnormal noises during the guarded test run.
- All records are completed and linked to the work order, and any deviations are entered into the corrective action system referenced in MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2.

Revision and change control
Refer to MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2 for the revision history and SB-1022 for parts lists and replacement instructions. Any suggested changes to this manual should be submitted through the engineering change process and cross-referenced to SOP-P3-L3-03 for operational alignment.
